neighbours.label: gaining new members, customers or followers: attract/recruit/win over/compete for new people
fire: The gym is offering a free month to attract new members this spring.
Rival parties are competing for young voters in the suburbs.
The choir is always looking for new singers to join its rehearsals.
Rural hospitals find it hard to attract and keep good nurses.
The shop hopes its loyalty card will bring in new customers.
The startup is trying to recruit talented engineers from abroad.
Both sects sent preachers into the countryside to win converts.
A good website can keep attracting new clients long after it is built.
quiet: The gym is offering free towels to its members this spring.
Rival parties held their rallies in the suburbs last weekend.
The choir rehearses every Thursday evening in the church hall.
Rural hospitals are often far from the nearest city.
The shop sells its loyalty card at the front counter.
Bright colours attract insects to the flowers in the garden.
Both sects built small chapels in the countryside.
A strong magnet can attract nails from several centimetres away.

notes: Probe: 'competing for converts' 0.78, 'attract and keep doctors' 0.57, 'looking for new members' 0.54, 'attracting new customers' 0.54, 'win over young voters' 0.52. A physical 'attract' scored low (magnet 0.11, flowers attracting bees 0.14), so it tracks the meaning, not the word. Two near misses test the physical sense of 'attract'.
